paper_metadata.title: Shearable carbide reinforced refractory medium-entropy alloy with enhanced high-temperature strength and room-temperature compressive plasticity

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: Here, a Re0.1Hf0.25Ta1.85W0.2C0.25 refractory medium-entropy alloy was designed and fabricated by vacuum arc melting, forming a carbide-reinforced multiphase architecture

evidence.section: 2.1. Sample preparation
evidence.quote: The Re0.1Hf0.25Ta1.85W0.2C0.25 RMEA sample was prepared by vacuum arc melting using a DHL1250 vacuum arc furnace (SKY Technology Development Co., Ltd, China) in a high-purity argon atmosphere. The purities of Hf, Ta, W, and Re exceeded 99.95 wt%, while carbon was introduced as TaC powder (5 µm, 99.9 wt%), which was wrapped in Ta foil. The ingot was remelted at least six times to ensure chemical homogeneity.

evidence.section: 3.1. Phase composition and microstructure of the as-cast alloy
evidence.quote: the as-cast Re0.1Hf0.25Ta1.85W0.2C0.25 RMEA has no pronounced preferred orientation and consists of three phases: BCC solid solution (JCPDS card No. 04-003-6604), M2C-HCP carbide (JCPDS card No. 04-001-6329), and MC-FCC carbide (JCPDS card No. 03-065-8216).

attributes.composition: primarily Ta2C with Hf substitutionally dissolved

evidence.quote: Backscattered-electron SEM images (Fig. 2) reveal a divorced eutectic microstructure in which the carbide phases (M2C-HCP) form an interconnected three-dimensional skeleton surrounding the BCC matrix.

attributes.composition: HfC-based with partial Ta substitution, identified as (Hf,Ta)C

evidence.section: 4.2. Plastic deformation mechanisms of skeletal and plate-like carbides
evidence.quote: During room-temperature compression, the plate-like MC precipitates develop dense stacking faults (SFs) [Fig. 11(b–d)], demonstrating that they can be sheared and deform cooperatively with the BCC matrix.

evidence.section: 3.3. Fracture morphology and microstructure of the alloy after compressive deformation
evidence.quote: As shown in Fig. 9(c and d), dense dislocation structures are observed within the M2C-HCP carbides, whereas no distinct stacking-fault bands are identified in the analyzed TEM regions.

attributes.morphology: lamellar delamination accompanied by wrinkled tearing features, MAX-phase-like laminated fracture appearance

evidence.section: 3.3. Fracture morphology and microstructure of the alloy after compressive deformation
evidence.quote: the fracture surface of the room-temperature compressed specimen exhibits a pronounced lamellar fracture morphology. The carbides do not display the typical brittle fracture features commonly associated with ceramic phases (e.g., flat cleavage facets or intergranular separation). Instead, their fracture surfaces are dominated by lamellar delamination accompanied by wrinkled tearing features, giving rise to a MAX-phase-like laminated fracture appearance.

evidence.section: 3.3. Fracture morphology and microstructure of the alloy after compressive deformation
evidence.quote: Localized microcracks are observed within the divorced-eutectic M2C-HCP carbides.
